content:
A listener writes “My paranormal encounters lasted for several years, and they all seemed to begin with a Ouija board. Personally, I have never used one myself, but what happened to me is totally strange.

I was stationed with the Army in Washington, D.C., from 1987 to 1991. While living there, I moved off post with a couple of buddies. One day, we were invited to a party being thrown by some medics. They were always crazy, so naturally, we had to go! I went with my roommate and a couple who lived upstairs from me. The guy was also in my platoon.

When we arrived, everyone started asking about Loren, as they had no idea who he was. It turned out that Loren was my buddy from upstairs, who had come along with his girlfriend. He started saying, “I’m Loren, but who’s asking?”

Apparently, a couple of women at the party had been using a Ouija board, and they said the board had started talking about him. Keep in mind that we had never met these women before, and this was our first time at their party.

After asking a couple of questions, the board identified itself as Jonathon and made its presence known through a plant.

Bear with me here. I know this sounds strange.

Loren and his girlfriend had been out shopping and picked up a little plant at a roadside market. They brought it home, and we all laughed because we thought it looked like a dick-shaped plant or something out of Little Shop of Horrors. It was about six inches tall and nowhere near blooming.

According to the Ouija board, Jonathon had been involved in a love triangle and was allegedly murdered by a jealous husband sometime in the late 1700s or early 1800s. I can’t remember the exact time period.

Anyway, we finished partying and went home. After we settled into our apartment, Loren came running downstairs with the plant. It had gone from six inches tall and green to 18 inches tall and in full bloom.

Honest to God, I swear this happened. Otherwise, I wouldn’t be writing about it.

After that, all sorts of strange things started happening around the apartment. We heard knocks, lights turned on and off, and keys mysteriously disappeared.

At one point, our dog launched itself off the couch and chased something invisible across the living room. Whatever it was appeared to hide in the closet, with the dog close behind.

Another night, I went down to the basement to do laundry. When I came back upstairs, my roommate was smoking a cigarette. He told me the dog had just done the same thing again.

The knocking always came in threes. As you may know, some people interpret three knocks as a mockery of the Holy Trinity.

We finally decided to tear the plant apart, piss on it, and leave it in the backyard. Our paranormal activity stopped that night.

Or so we thought.

I left the Army in 1991 and returned to college in Wisconsin. While there, I joined a fraternity and moved in with a fraternity brother.

One night, during an after-bar party, two of my female friends started using his Ouija board. I had no idea he even owned one. They began asking questions like, “Is anybody out there?” and “Do you know anyone in the room?” The board answered yes.

I told them to stop playing with it, but they started laughing. They continued asking questions, and when they asked about me by name, the board said it knew me.

When they asked how, I told them to stop, but they wouldn’t listen.

The board then spelled out P-L-A-N-T.

I told them not to continue.

They asked about the plant, and the board spelled out H-A-U-N-T-E-D.

At that point, I got up and kicked the board off their laps. They had been sitting with their knees touching while using it. They started freaking out, and I explained what had happened to us in Washington, D.C. That only made them more frightened.

We ended up staying in the dorms that night instead of returning to the house.

Not only did the knocking start again, but we also began hearing something walking through the house at odd times. You would hear footsteps approaching from somewhere out of view. When you looked up to see who it was, nobody would be there.

This happened at least half a dozen times. The following year, I moved into a new apartment. While living there, I was making chili. I left the can opener on the counter while I poured the beans into the pot. I can make it either way, after all!

When I went to pick up the can opener, it was gone.

I methodically searched the entire kitchen, checking every cabinet and drawer. Nothing.

I finally sat down in the living room and watched ESPN for about ten minutes. When I went back into the kitchen, the can opener was sitting right where I had left it.

No shit.

Nothing much happened after that until I got married.

First, I was visiting my dad in Washington State. I told him the same story, and my stepmother at the time told me about how she could leave her body and see what was happening around the orange orchard where she had grown up. She said she would then ask her father what he had been doing while she was watching him, even though he had never seen her.

Later, I was downstairs in the basement getting ready for bed when the light suddenly snapped off. It was on a 30-amp circuit with only one light connected to it, so there shouldn’t have been enough of a load to trip the breaker.

It was pretty strange.

I also experienced paranormal activity in an old house I once lived in. The house was built in 1895, and strange things happened there regularly. Lights turned on and off, I heard voices, and there was even the sound of something coughing. Occasionally, I would catch a whiff of an old, stale cigar smell.

I eventually learned that a man who had lived there long before me had suffered a heart attack and been found in the living room. He had been a cigar smoker. After my mother passed away, I would sometimes smell her perfume on Sunday mornings, as though she were visiting me.

My youngest son also had a strange experience in that house. As he was heading upstairs, a set of boots was thrown behind him as he walked through the kitchen.

Another night, he walked past the television while it was turned off. As he passed it, the TV suddenly switched on.

He said, “Nope!” He wasn’t even turning around to look at that one.

Later, I married my second wife, and we moved about half an hour north to a bar we had converted into our home.

While we were still operating the bar, I was in the kitchen when I saw a full-blown apparition come up the stairwell. It looked directly at me and then disappeared. We would also hear footsteps throughout the bar at night while we were cleaning up. This happened a lot.

It turned out that one of the original owners had suffered a heart attack in the backyard, where he was eventually found.

Looking back, the whole time I experienced these things, nothing ever seemed particularly evil or threatening. But they certainly made the hair stand up on the back of my neck.

It has been a pretty crazy ride at times, that’s for sure.”
